context_pill: Diversion of Income by Overriding Title
example_summary: MKG Agency partnership firm makes a payment of 20% of profits amounting to ₹ 1 lakh to the mother in March 2025 following the father's death, claiming it as a deduction for 2025-26.
source_provision:
### Statutory Framework: Diversion vs Application of Income

| Feature | Diversion of Income by Overriding Title | Application of Income |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Point of Legal Transfer** | Diverted at source **before** reaching the assessee. | Applied **after** reaching/accruing to the assessee. |
| **Nature of Obligation** | Pre-existing enforceable charge attached to the income source. | Voluntary or contractual obligation created post-accrual. |
| **Title to Income** | Third party holds a superior legal title to the income. | Assessee holds full title before applying the funds. |
| **Tax Consequence** | Excluded from the Total Income of the assessee. | Included in Total Income; no deduction allowed. |


#### Key Statutory Criteria for Overriding Title

* **Enforceable Legal Instrument:** The obligation must be created by a statute, court decree, or binding contract (e.g., Partnership Deed).
* **Charge on Source:** The obligation must bind the income at its source, preventing it from legally accruing as the assessee's income.


> [!IMPORTANT] Supreme Court & High Court Benchmarks
> * **CIT v. Sitaldas Tirathdas (1961) 41 ITR 367 (SC):** True test is whether the obligation diverts income before it reaches the assessee, or whether it is an obligation to apply income after it has accrued.
> * **CIT v. Nariman B. Bharucha & Sons (1981) 130 ITR 863 (Bom):** Payments made to third parties pursuant to a charge created on profits by a partnership deed constitute diversion of income by overriding title and are excluded from the firm's total income.

director.justification: The core legal issue is classifying the payment as either a diversion of income by overriding title or a mere application of income based on the partnership deed's terms.
director.visual_metaphor: A river with a pre-built canal that redirects 20% of the water before it ever reaches the main reservoir.
